aliases: methodes nouvelles de la mecanique celeste

evidence.claim: Poincare published a note on curves defined by a differential equation (qualitative, geometric study of orbits) in 1880.
Memoir of the same title appears in the 1881 and 1882 volumes of J. Math. Pures Appl.

conceptual.note: Earliest indexed publication of the geometric/qualitative programme. Later instalments (1885-86) were not searched, so the end year is the last one found, not the last one that exists.

evidence.claim: Poincare applied topological and qualitative methods to the restricted three-body problem in the Acta Mathematica memoir of 1890.
evidence.source: zbMATH Open record 2690614 (English title: On the three-body problem and the equations of dynamics); Crossref DOI record of Acta Math. 13 (1890)

evidence.claim: Volume III of Les methodes nouvelles (1899) discusses doubly asymptotic (homoclinic) solutions in the text.
evidence.source: Les methodes nouvelles de la mecanique celeste, t. III, 1899 (archive.org full text)

methodological.note: Memoir was a prize entry (1888); I did not verify from a record that an error was found and corrected before the 1890 printing (commonly told, not checked here). The Crossref title for the DOI is just Introduction (chapter-level record). Homoclinic intersections are treated at length in vol. III (1899).

evidence.claim: Birkhoff, Quelques theoremes sur le mouvement des systemes dynamiques, Bull. SMF 1912: earliest indexed title found naming dynamical systems as an object.
Birkhoff monograph Dynamical Systems, AMS Colloquium Publications vol. 9, 1927.

institutional.note: Corpus: zbMATH Open title search for dynamical (1850-1911) returned only physics/gas-theory titles; search for systemes dynamiques (1880-1935) gave 1912 first. 1927 is the first named monograph. Not searched: ICM sections, MSC code 37, chairs.

works.citation: Sur le probleme des trois corps et les equations de la dynamique, Acta Math. 13 (1890)
works.whyItMatters: Geometric treatment of the restricted three-body problem; homoclinic phenomena.

works.citation: Les methodes nouvelles de la mecanique celeste, t. III (Gauthier-Villars)
works.whyItMatters: Systematic account including doubly asymptotic solutions.

works.citation: Proof of Poincare's geometric theorem, Trans. AMS 14
works.whyItMatters: Proved Poincare last geometric theorem, a founding result of the field.

works.citation: Dynamical Systems, AMS Colloquium Publications 9
works.whyItMatters: First named monograph; recasts celestial mechanics as general dynamics.

notes: Source summary said Birkhoff built on Poincare; confirmed by the 1913 and 1927 records above.
Priority and error story around the 1889-90 memoir not checked here.

evidence.claim: Frechet, Sur quelques points du calcul fonctionnel, Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo 22 (1906): abstract-space framework for function sets.

conceptual.note: This is his thesis paper. I did not read the text, so the claim that it contains the full metric-space axioms rests on the standard account plus the title and date.

evidence.claim: Same 1906 paper is aimed at function spaces (calcul fonctionnel); Frechet 1910 follow-up on abstract sets and functional calculus.

methodological.note: Use of the abstract-space tool on a function-space target is in the founding paper itself, so the two dates coincide. Not separately verified from text.

evidence.claim: Hausdorff, Grundzuege der Mengenlehre (Leipzig, 1914): first monograph treating metric spaces as a named concept; text uses metrischer Raum.
evidence.source: archive.org full text of the 1914 edition; zbMATH Open record 2615204

evidence.claim: Frechet, Les espaces abstraits ... introduction a lanalyse generale, 1928.

institutional.note: Earlier paper titles by Frechet (1906, 1910) name abstract sets/functional calculus, not metric spaces. Menger Untersuchungen ueber allgemeine Metrik (Math. Ann. 1928, DOI 10.1007/bf01448840) is a later named series. Hausdorff text also discusses Frechet limit-based theory.

works.citation: Sur quelques points du calcul fonctionnel, Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo 22
works.whyItMatters: Introduces the abstract-space setting for function spaces.

works.citation: Les ensembles abstraits et le calcul fonctionnel, Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo 30
works.whyItMatters: Extends the programme of abstract sets applied to functional calculus.

works.citation: Grundzuege der Mengenlehre
works.whyItMatters: Names and systematises metric spaces inside general topology.

notes: I did not check the exact term Frechet used in 1906 (I recall classes with an ecart/distance, unverified).
Earlier work by Cantor, Volterra, Arzela and Hadamard named in the event summary was not searched.

evidence.claim: Langlands, Problems in the theory of automorphic forms, Lecture Notes in Math. 170 (1970): earliest published statement of the conjectures found.
evidence.source: Crossref DOI record; zbMATH Open record 3356942

evidence.claim: Langlands wrote Weil a 17-page letter in January 1967 sketching the conjectures; typed copies circulated.

conceptual.note: Private letter to Weil, January 1967, precedes publication (kept here, not used as the date). Jacquet-Langlands, Automorphic forms on GL(2) (LNM 114, 1970, DOI 10.1007/BFb0058988) is contemporaneous. I did not exclude earlier printed lecture notes or the Yale Euler products notes (zbMATH lists 1971).

evidence.claim: Tunnell, Artins conjecture for representations of octahedral type, Bull. AMS 5 (1981): treats an Artin L-function case via the Langlands approach.

methodological.note: Judgement call: first purposeful use of the correspondence to settle a target problem is taken as Langlands-Tunnell (base change, Langlands 1980, plus Tunnell 1981). Jacquet-Langlands 1970 and Drinfeld 1977 (function fields, see P057) may count as earlier uses; the link between title and method is inferred, not read from text.

evidence.claim: Gelbart, An elementary introduction to the Langlands program, Bull. AMS 10 (1984): earliest indexed title with the phrase Langlands program.
Langlands, Automorphic representations, Shimura varieties, and motives. Ein Maerchen, Proc. Symp. Pure Math. 33 (1979).

institutional.note: Corpus: zbMATH Open title searches Langlands program (1975-1989), Langlands conjectures (1970-1985), Langlands correspondence (1970-1990). Earlier titles mentioning Langlands (Godement 1968, 1971; Schmid 1971) concern his Eisenstein series, Euler products or a different conjecture and are not counted. MSC code (11F70 etc.) and Corvallis conference not verified.

works.citation: Problems in the theory of automorphic forms, LNM 170
works.whyItMatters: First published formulation.

works.citation: Automorphic representations, Shimura varieties, and motives. Ein Maerchen
works.whyItMatters: Broad statement of functoriality and motives.

works.citation: Automorphic forms on GL(2), LNM 114 (with Langlands)
works.whyItMatters: Builds the GL(2) theory linking automorphic and Galois side.

works.citation: Proof of the global Langlands conjecture for GL(2) over a function field, Funct. Anal. Appl. 11
works.whyItMatters: First proof of a global case.

notes: Weil letter (Jan 1967) is the usual private origin; kept as a note.
Whether Langlands-Tunnell or Jacquet-Langlands is the first purposeful use is a judgement call.
Jacquet birth year taken from standard reference, not checked in a fetched page.

canonicalName: Formal language theory (Chomsky hierarchy and automata)

evidence.claim: Chomsky, Three models for the description of language, IRE Trans. Information Theory (Sept 1956): compares finite-state, phrase-structure, transformational models.
Kleene, Representation of events in nerve nets and finite automata, in Automata Studies (1956).

conceptual.note: Full hierarchy with types 0-3 linked to machine classes comes in Chomsky 1959 (Information and Control, DOI 10.1016/S0019-9958(59)90362-6); the 1956 paper contains the ordering of grammar models only. Kleene 1956 independently gives finite automata and regular events.

evidence.claim: Same 1956 paper applies finite-state models to natural language and judges them inadequate.
Chomsky and Miller, Finite state languages, Information and Control 1958.

methodological.note: Claim about the content of the 1956 paper rests on its title and standard account; I did not read the text.

evidence.claim: Chomsky, On certain formal properties of grammars, Information and Control 2 (1959): earliest indexed title found pairing formal with grammars.
Ginsburg, The mathematical theory of context-free languages (1966).
Hopcroft and Ullman, Formal languages and their relation to automata (1969): first textbook with formal languages in the title found.

institutional.note: Corpus: zbMATH Open title search formal languages (1955-1965) returned 1960 first (Bar-Hillel and Shamir, formal representations), formal language (1950-1962) returned no hits. Dates here are earliest indexed titles only; journal founding, MSC 68Q45 and chairs not searched.

works.citation: Three models for the description of language, IRE Trans. Inf. Theory 2
works.whyItMatters: Introduces the comparison of grammar types.

works.citation: On certain formal properties of grammars, Information and Control 2
works.whyItMatters: Gives the grammar hierarchy.

works.citation: The algebraic theory of context-free languages (with Chomsky)
works.whyItMatters: Algebraic treatment linking grammars and formal power series.

works.citation: Representation of events in nerve nets and finite automata, Automata Studies
works.whyItMatters: Equates finite automata with regular events.

notes: No firstTermUse given: no title record supports a specific first use of formal language.
Chomsky-Schutzenberger 1963 is what I would call the systematisation of the algebraic side.
Lifespans for Kleene, Schutzenberger from MacTutor pages (status checked: URLs resolve).

canonicalName: Fuchs-Frobenius theory of regular singular points
aliases: Fuchs theory of linear differential equations

evidence.claim: Fuchs, Zur Theorie der linearen Differentialgleichungen mit veraenderlichen Coefficienten, J. reine angew. Math. 66 (1866) 121-160.
evidence.source: Crossref DOI record; zbMATH Open record 2750068

conceptual.note: Fuchs 1868 addendum (zbMATH 2750007) also exists. Predecessors (Riemann on the hypergeometric equation, Briot-Bouquet) were searched in zbMATH but not confirmed, so not used.

evidence.claim: Frobenius, Ueber die Integration der linearen Differentialgleichungen durch Reihen, Crelle 76 (1873).
evidence.source: Crossref DOI record; zbMATH Open record 2717950

methodological.note: Judgement call: Fuchs 1866 already uses complex-function methods on the equations; 1873 is when the series method for regular singular points is applied systematically. Frobenius 1875 on regular solutions (zbMATH 2715353) continues it.

evidence.claim: Heffter, Einleitung in die Theorie der linearen Differentialgleichungen (1894).
Schlesinger, Handbuch der Theorie der linearen Differentialgleichungen, vol. I (1895).

institutional.note: These are the earliest textbooks found in zbMATH for the linear-ODE theory; they do not name Fuchs or Frobenius in the title. Fuchsian functions (Poincare, 1880-84; zbMATH 2706679 etc.) are a different object named after Fuchs. No title naming the Frobenius method was found.

works.citation: Zur Theorie der linearen Differentialgleichungen mit veraenderlichen Coefficienten, Crelle 66
works.whyItMatters: Defines the class with regular singular points.

works.citation: Ueber die Integration der linearen Differentialgleichungen durch Reihen, Crelle 76
works.whyItMatters: The series method now called by his name.

notes: Lifespans from MacTutor-style references; the pages resolve but I did not re-read dates there.

evidence.claim: Cotes, Logometria, Phil. Trans. 29(338), March 1714; the logarithm of a quantity of form cosine plus root of minus one times sine is stated in geometric language (see p. 32).
evidence.source: Crossref DOI record; Wikipedia Euler formula history cites p. 32

evidence.claim: Cotes published only one paper in his lifetime, Logometria, March 1714.

conceptual.note: Statement is geometric; reading it as the modern identity needs a sign correction (secondary source). I did not read the Latin text myself. Euler gave the exponential form in Introductio (1748) and Johann Bernoulli worked with imaginary logarithms around 1702; neither checked here.

evidence.claim: Logometria is a work on logarithmic quadratures; the identity is used to express circular arcs via logarithms.

methodological.note: Weak: no source read that demonstrates a distinct target problem solved with the identity. Kept low.

evidence.claim: Thomae, Abriss einer Theorie der complexen Functionen (1870): earliest indexed title found for a theory of complex functions.

institutional.note: Corpus: zbMATH Open title searches for complexen Veraenderlichen, Functionentheorie (1860-1880). Durege textbook first edition is later than 1860 but only its 1873 and later editions were seen. Complex analysis was named in many ways earlier (Cauchy memoirs); this is an indexed-title floor only.

works.citation: Logometria, Phil. Trans. 29(338)
works.whyItMatters: Contains the geometric form of the logarithm of a complex argument.

works.citation: Harmonia mensurarum (ed. R. Smith), Cambridge
works.whyItMatters: Posthumous collection reprinting Logometria.

works.citation: Introductio in analysin infinitorum
works.whyItMatters: Gives the exponential-form identity (zbMATH lists the Opera omnia edition; original 1748 not directly cited).

notes: Priority: Cotes 1714 geometric statement vs Euler 1748 analytic formula; Bernoulli 1702 not verified.
Euler work record is for the Opera omnia volume (1922), not the 1748 original.

evidence.claim: Euclid compiled the Elements in the time of the first Ptolemy (per Proclus); dated here by his approximate lifespan, c. 325 to c. 265 BC.
Hippocrates of Chios (c. 470 to c. 410 BC) is recorded as the first to compile an Elements; it is lost.
evidence.source: MacTutor biography of Hippocrates, quoting Proclus

conceptual.note: No bibliographic record exists for ancient publication; the range is the author lifespan, not a publication date. Priority: an earlier lost Elements by Hippocrates; Proclus says Euclid also reordered Eudoxus and Theaetetus.

evidence.claim: Euclid arranged earlier results as proofs in order.

methodological.note: The treatise itself is the first extant deductive application; coincides with the conceptual date. No finer evidence.

evidence.claim: Euclid title Elements (Stoicheia) for the treatise.

institutional.note: Earliest manuscripts, Heiberg edition (1883-88) and Heath translation (1908) are modern; I did not search manuscript evidence.

works.citation: Elements, ed. J. L. Heiberg in Euclidis Opera omnia, vol. 1 (Teubner)
works.whyItMatters: Standard critical edition of the Greek text.

works.citation: The Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements, trans. T. L. Heath
works.whyItMatters: Standard English translation with commentary.

notes: Hippocrates of Chios omitted from people: his work is lost and no work record found.
Precise date unevidenced; range derives from lifespan only.

canonicalName: Boolean algebra: logic as algebra, then Stone duality

evidence.claim: Boole, The Mathematical Analysis of Logic (Cambridge, 1847).
evidence.source: Open Library work record (first publication 1847); archive.org scan

evidence.claim: Boole, An Investigation of the Laws of Thought (1854).

conceptual.note: Stone duality statement is later (1934-36); the idea of logic as algebra is 1847. Jevons and Peirce reworked it later.

evidence.claim: Stone, Boolean algebras and their application to topology, PNAS 20 (1934).
Stone, The theory of representations for Boolean algebras, Trans. AMS 40 (1936).

methodological.note: Methodological taken as use of Boolean algebra against topology (Stone). Titles seen; text not read.

evidence.claim: Peirce, On the algebra of logic, Amer. J. Math. 3 (1880): earliest indexed title found.
Schroeder, Vorlesungen ueber die Algebra der Logik, vol. I (1890).
Huntington, Sets of independent postulates for the algebra of logic, Trans. AMS (1904).
Sheffer, A set of five independent postulates for Boolean algebras, Trans. AMS (1913).

institutional.note: Corpus: zbMATH Open title search algebra of logic (1860-1900) and Boolean algebra (1860-1925). The earliest Boolean algebras in a title I found is Sheffer 1913. Earlier Peirce papers (1867 proceedings) were seen in Crossref with a date mismatch and not used.

works.citation: The Mathematical Analysis of Logic
works.whyItMatters: Logic treated as an algebra.

works.citation: An Investigation of the Laws of Thought
works.whyItMatters: Full development and probabilities.

works.citation: Vorlesungen ueber die Algebra der Logik, vol. I
works.whyItMatters: Systematic treatise.

works.citation: Sets of independent postulates for the algebra of logic, Trans. AMS 5
works.whyItMatters: Axiomatises the structure.

works.citation: Boolean algebras and their application to topology, PNAS 20
works.whyItMatters: Opens the topological dictionary.

works.citation: The theory of representations for Boolean algebras, Trans. AMS 40
works.whyItMatters: Stone representation theorem.

notes: Boolean algebra proper (axioms) is only fixed by Huntington 1904 and Sheffer 1913.
Stone dates cover several papers (1934, 1935, 1936).

aliases: Langlands for GL(n) over function fields

evidence.claim: Drinfeld, Elliptic modules, Mat. Sb. 94 (1974); introduces Drinfeld modules as a tool for function-field arithmetic.

conceptual.note: Whether the 1974 paper states the Langlands link for GL(2) was not read; the explicit Langlands claim is dated 1977 under methodological.

evidence.claim: Drinfeld, Proof of the global Langlands conjecture for GL(2) over a function field, Funct. Anal. Appl. 11 (1977).
Lafforgue, Chtoucas de Drinfeld et correspondance de Langlands, Invent. Math. 147 (2002): GL(n) case.

methodological.note: GL(2) in 1977 (shtuka-based approach announced; full account in Drinfeld 1987-89 F-sheaves papers, J. Soviet Math record DOI 10.1007/BF01099348); GL(n) by Lafforgue 2002.

evidence.claim: 1977 paper title names the Langlands conjecture over a function field.
Fields Medal to L. Lafforgue, ICM Beijing, 20 August 2002.

institutional.note: Corpus: zbMATH Open title searches Drinfeld modules (1970-1990), Drinfeld shtukas, Langlands plus function field. Drinfeld modules title earliest found: Yu 1983. Drinfeld ICM 1978 talk (zbMATH 3693404, listed 1980) not verified by date. No dedicated chair or MSC checked.

works.citation: Elliptic modules, Math. USSR Sb. 23
works.whyItMatters: Introduces the objects.

works.citation: Proof of the global Langlands conjecture for GL(2) over a function field, Funct. Anal. Appl. 11
works.whyItMatters: First proof of a global case.

works.citation: Chtoucas de Drinfeld et correspondance de Langlands, Invent. Math. 147
works.whyItMatters: Proves GL(n).

works.citation: Une compactification des champs classifiant les chtoucas de Drinfeld, JAMS 11
works.whyItMatters: Compactification used in the proof.

notes: First-term evidence is a zbMATH record (Kazhdan 1979 title), earliest found only.
Interpretation of 1974 vs 1977 as conceptual vs methodological is a judgement call.

canonicalName: Murmurations of elliptic curves and L-functions

evidence.claim: He, Lee, Oliver, Pozdnyakov, Murmurations of elliptic curves, arXiv 2204.10140, posted April 2022.
Same paper published in Experimental Mathematics, 2024.
Alessandretti, Baronchelli, He, ML meets number theory: BSD data science, arXiv 1911.02008 (Nov 2019): ML on elliptic-curve data.
He, Lee, Oliver, Machine-learning the Sato-Tate conjecture, arXiv 2010.01213 (2020).

methodological.note: Earliest ML-on-elliptic-curves paper found; murmurations discovery in the 2022 preprint is itself an application of the tool, so the target is arguable. Only searched arXiv and Crossref.

evidence.claim: Preprint title Murmurations of elliptic curves, 2022; later Zubrilina, Murmurations, arXiv 2310.07681 (2023).

institutional.note: Earliest indexed title only. Conferences, MSC codes, chairs not searched. zbMATH shows later follow-up papers (2025-2026).

works.citation: Murmurations of elliptic curves, Exp. Math. (with Lee, Oliver, Pozdnyakov)
works.whyItMatters: Discovery of the pattern.

works.citation: Machine learning meets number theory: the data science of BSD
works.whyItMatters: Earlier ML-on-elliptic-curves work.

works.citation: Murmurations of Dirichlet characters, IMRN (with Oliver, Pozdnyakov)
works.whyItMatters: Extends the phenomenon to Dirichlet characters.

notes: Zubrilina (Inventiones 2025, DOI 10.1007/s00222-025-01347-8) explained murmurations for modular forms; omitted from people because no biography URL was found.
Pozdnyakov and Oliver omitted for the same reason.
Conceptual vs methodological dates depend on whether the 2019 ML work counts.
